sentences.en: The singer Kali Simon has suffered for most of her life from stage fright.
sentences.zh: 歌手卡莉·西蒙大半辈子都深受舞台恐惧症的困扰。

sentences.en: Although she enjoys performing in front of an audience,

sentences.en: she never knows when a surge of panic will bring her to her knees.
sentences.zh: 但她永远不知道什么时候一阵恐慌会让她瘫倒在地。

sentences.en: In 1981, she set out to conquer her fear
sentences.zh: 1981年，她决定克服这种恐惧，

sentences.en: by arranging a string of concert dates at big concert halls.
sentences.zh: 于是安排了一系列大型音乐厅的巡演。

sentences.en: Midway through the tour, during the first of two shows in Pittsburgh,
sentences.zh: 巡演进行到一半时，在匹兹堡两场演出中的第一场，

sentences.en: she felt her heart begin to race.
sentences.zh: 她感到自己的心跳开始加速。

sentences.en: Carly Simon told the audience what was happening.
sentences.zh: 卡莉·西蒙告诉了观众发生了什么。

sentences.en: Go with it, they called to her.
sentences.zh: “顺其自然吧，”他们对她喊道。

sentences.en: We'll be with you.
sentences.zh: “我们会陪着你。”

sentences.en: She invited some fans to join her on the stage for support.
sentences.zh: 她邀请了一些粉丝上台支持她。

sentences.en: They huddled around her, rubbing her arms and legs
sentences.zh: 他们围在她身边，揉着她的手臂和腿，

sentences.en: and telling her that they loved her.
sentences.zh: 告诉她他们爱她。

sentences.en: She was able to finish that show.
sentences.zh: 她最终完成了那场演出。

sentences.en: But right before the next show,
sentences.zh: 但在下一场演出前夕，

sentences.en: with 10,000 people waiting to see her perform,
sentences.zh: 面对一万名等待她表演的观众，

sentences.en: she collapsed.

sentences.en: She canceled the rest of the tour
sentences.zh: 她取消了剩余的巡演，

sentences.en: and stopped performing in public.
sentences.zh: 并停止了公开表演。

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain,

sentences.en: from doing the things we want to do.
sentences.zh: 让我们无法去做自己想做的事。

sentences.zh: 研究恐惧心理学，

sentences.en: how it helps us, how it hurts us,

sentences.en: If you peer down the long corridors of evolution,
sentences.zh: 如果你审视漫长的进化长廊，

sentences.en: you will see that there are many aspects of the brain that have changed over time.
sentences.zh: 你会发现大脑中有许多方面随着时间的推移发生了变化。

sentences.en: But researchers find that the neural pathways that govern fear
sentences.zh: 但研究人员发现，支配恐惧的神经通路

sentences.en: are highly preserved across species.
sentences.zh: 在不同物种间高度保守。

sentences.en: You can find them in rodents, in antelopes, and in humans.
sentences.zh: 你可以在啮齿动物、羚羊和人类身上找到它们。

sentences.en: There is a simple reason for this.
sentences.zh: 这背后的原因很简单。

sentences.en: Creatures who lack the capacity for fear did reckless things
sentences.zh: 缺乏恐惧能力的生物会做出鲁莽的行为，

sentences.en: and were quickly removed from the gene pool.
sentences.zh: 并很快被从基因库中淘汰。

sentences.en: The survivors were the ones who had a healthy capacity for fear,
sentences.zh: 幸存者是那些拥有健全恐惧能力的人，

sentences.en: and they passed their genes to us.
sentences.zh: 他们将基因传给了我们。

sentences.en: But what this means is that we all have fear circuits in our brains
sentences.zh: 但这意味着我们所有人的大脑中都有恐惧回路，

sentences.en: that were sculpted in the Stone Age.

sentences.en: What worked for our ancestors may not always work for us.
sentences.zh: 对我们祖先有效的方法，对我们来说未必总是有效。

sentences.en: Psychiatrist Arash Javanbakh has studied what fear does to us.
sentences.zh: 精神病学家阿拉什·贾万巴赫（Arash Javanbakh）研究了恐惧对我们的影响。

sentences.en: He believes that understanding the mechanisms of fear
sentences.zh: 他认为，理解恐惧的机制

sentences.en: can help us form a wiser relationship with this ancient emotion.
sentences.zh: 可以帮助我们与这种古老的情绪建立更明智的关系。

sentences.en: Arash, I understand that a number of years ago, you were sitting in your parked car when
sentences.zh: 阿拉什，我听说几年前，你坐在停着的车里时，

sentences.en: something very dramatic happened to you.
sentences.zh: 发生了一件非常戏剧性的事情。

sentences.en: Tell me what happened.
sentences.zh: 告诉我发生了什么。

sentences.en: So this happened early in medical school.
sentences.zh: 那是医学院早期发生的事。

sentences.en: We were near the university hospital with a few of my classmates.
sentences.zh: 当时我和几位同学在大学医院附近。

sentences.en: We were getting ready to go to funeral of one of our classmates' mother.
sentences.zh: 我们正准备去参加一位同学母亲的葬礼。

sentences.en: and all of a sudden this motorcycle riding very fast just plows through the driver's side door
sentences.zh: 突然，一辆飞驰的摩托车直接撞穿了驾驶座一侧的车门。

sentences.en: wow and i'm so happy nobody was injured luckily and miraculously but basically the two doors on
sentences.zh: 哇，我很庆幸没人受伤，这真是幸运且奇迹般，但基本上左侧的两个车门完全损毁了，但我记得当时的情景就像是在看一部慢动作电影。

sentences.en: the left were just totally damaged but what i remember was it's as if i'm seeing a slow motion
sentences.zh: 电影。

sentences.en: movie.
sentences.zh: 电影。

sentences.en: And right now, 20-some years later, you and I are talking, I see the image right in front of
sentences.zh: 现在，二十多年过去了，你和我正在交谈，我依然能清晰地看到眼前的画面。

sentences.en: me.
sentences.zh: 我看到那辆摩托车缓慢地向我驶来，基本上是慢动作，我全神贯注。

sentences.en: And I see how slowly that bike is coming towards me, basically slow motion with full
sentences.zh: 我看到那辆摩托车缓慢地向我驶来，基本上是慢动作，我全神贯注。

sentences.en: attention.
sentences.zh: 我全神贯注。

sentences.en: And then I saw, even I remember the guy's face as the bike was getting closer and
sentences.zh: 然后我看到了，甚至记得摩托车靠近并撞上我这边车门时那个人的脸。

sentences.en: hit the door on my side.
sentences.zh: 撞上我这边车门。

sentences.en: So you clearly had a chance to look up and see him coming toward you.
sentences.zh: 所以你显然有机会抬头看到他向你冲过来。

sentences.en: I'm assuming you didn't have enough time at this point to actually get out of the way or start the car or move the car.
sentences.zh: 我猜你当时没有足够的时间躲避、发动汽车或移动车辆。

sentences.en: What you're describing happening in slow motion, of course, probably happened in a couple of seconds or even a fraction of a second.
sentences.zh: 你描述的这种慢动作感，当然，可能只发生在几秒钟甚至一秒钟之内。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: I couldn't do anything.
sentences.zh: 我什么也做不了。

sentences.en: The car wasn't even on.
sentences.zh: 车甚至都没发动。

sentences.en: And I just saw a scared face and then boom.
sentences.zh: 我只看到一张惊恐的脸，然后砰的一声。

sentences.en: That was all I saw, but in a very slow motion
sentences.zh: 那就是我所看到的一切，但过程非常缓慢，

sentences.en: and being aware of all the, even the colors of what's going on around,
sentences.zh: 而且我意识到了周围的一切，甚至包括周围事物的颜色，

sentences.en: what time of the day was.
sentences.zh: 当时的时间。

sentences.en: Basically, my brain registered all the context and accused that were there.
sentences.zh: 基本上，我的大脑记录了当时所有的背景和线索。

sentences.en: So why does this happen, Arash?
sentences.zh: 那么，阿拉什，为什么会这样呢？

sentences.en: When we have these very dramatic things happen to us,
sentences.zh: 当我们经历这些非常戏剧性的事情时，

sentences.en: I think many of us have these moments that almost feel cinematic,
sentences.zh: 我想我们许多人都有过这种近乎电影般的时刻，

sentences.en: where everything seems to slow down and we can see things in great clarity,
sentences.zh: 一切似乎都慢了下来，我们可以极其清晰地看到事物，

sentences.en: but there's nothing that we can do about it.
sentences.zh: 但我们却无能为力。

sentences.en: Why do you think this is happening?
sentences.zh: 你认为这是为什么？

sentences.en: What is happening inside our brains?
sentences.zh: 我们的大脑内部发生了什么？

sentences.en: So fear has a very long story with us,
sentences.zh: 恐惧与我们有着很长的渊源，

sentences.en: and we have to understand the context within which it evolved.
sentences.zh: 我们必须了解它进化的背景。

sentences.en: And the context within which fear evolved was a context of physical threats.
sentences.zh: 恐惧进化的背景是物理威胁。

sentences.en: We had to worry about a predator or another human attacking us
sentences.zh: 我们必须担心捕食者、其他人类的攻击，

sentences.en: or a falling rock or natural disaster.
sentences.zh: 或是落石、自然灾害。

sentences.en: So the system is designed to react very fast to the dangers that are around us.
sentences.zh: 所以这个系统旨在对周围的危险做出极快的反应。

sentences.en: And when the system is activated, the brain regions involved in fear processing, including the amygdala and the sympathetic nervous system,
sentences.zh: 当系统被激活时，大脑中参与恐惧处理的区域，包括杏仁核和交感神经系统，

sentences.en: basically it was not that the environment slowed down.
sentences.zh: 其实并不是环境变慢了，

sentences.en: I sped up.
sentences.zh: 而是我变快了。

sentences.en: So my processing speeds up, my attention becomes hyper-focused, and the memory becomes stronger.
sentences.zh: 我的处理速度加快了，注意力变得高度集中，记忆也变得更强。

sentences.en: So we register such experiences even more crisp and more strongly.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们对这类经历的记录更加清晰、更加深刻。

sentences.en: And that by itself has an evolutionary purpose.
sentences.zh: 这本身就具有进化的目的。

sentences.en: because if something is dangerous if something is a threat I should register and learn it so well
sentences.zh: 因为如果某件事是危险的，是威胁，我就应该记录并深刻学习它，

sentences.en: that the next time if this is about to happen let's say instead of the motorcycle approaching me very
sentences.zh: 这样下次如果类似的事情要发生——比方说，不是摩托车飞速向我冲来，

sentences.en: fast it was a grizzly bear and I was attacked by a bear as a tribal human 50,000 years ago
sentences.zh: 而是5万年前作为部落人类的我被灰熊袭击了，

sentences.en: it would be very dumb for me for the second time to go try to pet the next grizzly bear that I met
sentences.zh: 如果我第二次遇到灰熊还试图去抚摸它，那我就太蠢了。

sentences.en: So it registers in my brain so well that this is dangerous.
sentences.zh: 所以它在大脑中清晰地记录下这是危险的。

sentences.en: You got to be careful and also learn whatever skill you need to avoid it the next time.
sentences.zh: 你必须小心，并学习下次避免它所需的任何技能。

sentences.en: Orash, when you describe the motorcycle approach in slow motion, it sounded like you were frozen in place.
sentences.zh: 阿拉什，当你描述摩托车慢动作冲过来时，听起来你当时僵住了。

sentences.en: You couldn't do anything but watch the crash unfold.
sentences.zh: 你除了看着车祸发生，什么也做不了。

sentences.en: Why does the sense of paralysis sometimes strike us when we feel very afraid?
sentences.zh: 为什么当我们感到极度恐惧时，有时会产生这种瘫痪感？

sentences.en: And that's another amazing aspect of fear.
sentences.zh: 这也是恐惧的另一个惊人之处。

sentences.en: So we have the fight response, flight response, and the freeze response.
sentences.zh: 我们有战斗反应、逃跑反应和僵直反应。

sentences.en: Freeze response has been seen mostly in animals which are preys.
sentences.zh: 僵直反应主要见于作为猎物的动物身上。

sentences.en: For example, a rabbit spots a hawk, and the rabbit freezes because it doesn't want to be seen.
sentences.zh: 例如，兔子发现了一只鹰，它会僵住，因为它不想被发现。

sentences.en: So basically, the brain paralyzes the system, so the motion is minimal.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，大脑会让系统瘫痪，从而将动作减到最少。

sentences.en: For humans, we are more of the predatorial animal, and that's why freeze response is less often observed.
sentences.zh: 对于人类来说，我们更偏向于捕食性动物，这就是为什么僵直反应较少见。

sentences.en: But when there is no other option, you try to basically minimize the risks and minimize the resources and minimize the chances of more harm by freezing.
sentences.zh: 但当没有其他选择时，你会通过僵直来尽量降低风险、减少资源消耗，并减少受到更多伤害的可能性。

sentences.en: And we see this reaction in a lot of horrible situations where humans are stuck, like rape and assault and torture, that they cannot do anything else.
sentences.zh: 我们在许多人类陷入困境的恐怖情况中都能看到这种反应，比如强奸、袭击和酷刑，他们无法做任何其他事情。

sentences.en: So the best option is to not do anything to at least, let's say, going back to the evolutionary context, reduce the amount of bleeding.
sentences.zh: 所以最好的选择就是什么都不做，至少，回到进化的背景来看，是为了减少出血量。

sentences.en: So you've given me some very dramatic examples where freezing happens.
sentences.zh: 你给了我一些非常戏剧性的僵直例子。

sentences.en: You know, a predator is attacking its prey or a human being is being attacked by another person.
sentences.zh: 你知道，捕食者攻击猎物，或者一个人被另一个人攻击。

sentences.en: Very dramatic situations.
sentences.zh: 非常戏剧性的情况。

sentences.en: Can freezing also happen in less dramatic situations, situations involving psychological peril?
sentences.zh: 僵直也会发生在不那么戏剧性的情况中吗，比如涉及心理危机的时刻？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对会。

sentences.en: We talked about how this system has evolved to react to very physical situations of danger.
sentences.zh: 我们谈到了这个系统是如何进化以应对非常具体的物理危险情况的。

sentences.en: But what you are coming to now is that in the modern life,
sentences.zh: 但你现在提到的是，在现代生活中，

sentences.en: majority of the threats that we are perceiving are so abstract.
sentences.zh: 我们感知到的大多数威胁都是非常抽象的。

sentences.en: A few years ago, we were talking about this virus,
sentences.zh: 几年前，我们谈论这种病毒，

sentences.en: which is spreading from China to Europe and gradually coming to America.
sentences.zh: 它从中国传播到欧洲，并逐渐来到美国。

sentences.en: It's a virus.
sentences.zh: 这是一种病毒。

sentences.en: We don't even see it.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至看不见它。

sentences.en: We just hear the news and we have to make decisions based on that.
sentences.zh: 我们只是听到新闻，然后必须据此做出决定。

sentences.en: So the system gets confused a lot of times.
sentences.zh: 所以这个系统经常会感到困惑。

sentences.en: But also, there are situations that you pause to be able to process more.
sentences.zh: 但也有一些情况，你会暂停以进行更多的处理。

sentences.en: You pause because you cannot do anything else.
sentences.zh: 你暂停是因为你无法做任何其他事情。

sentences.en: Or it's a better self-preservation to not make a move when you do not know what is the move to make.
sentences.zh: 或者在不知道该采取什么行动时，不采取行动是一种更好的自我保护。

sentences.en: In your work with many veterans, first responders, and refugees,
sentences.zh: 在你与许多退伍军人、急救人员和难民的工作中，

sentences.en: you say that sometimes what happens is that not only are we afraid of the thing that originally caused our fear,
sentences.zh: 你说有时发生的情况不仅是我们害怕最初导致恐惧的事物，

sentences.en: we start to generalize across similar things that might also be a trigger for our fear.
sentences.zh: 我们还开始将恐惧推广到可能成为恐惧触发因素的类似事物上。

sentences.en: And you see that many of these first responders and veterans often have frightening experiences when it comes to one holiday in the United States.
sentences.zh: 你发现许多急救人员和退伍军人在美国的一个节日里经常有可怕的经历。

sentences.en: What is that holiday, Arash?
sentences.zh: 阿拉什，那是什么节日？

sentences.en: Fourth of July.
sentences.zh: 独立日（7月4日）。

sentences.en: So this generalization of fear is, again, an evolutionary advantage.
sentences.zh: 所以这种恐惧的泛化，同样是一种进化优势。

sentences.en: As you said, a grizzly bear attacks me or one of my tribe mates.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，灰熊攻击了我或我的部落同伴。

sentences.en: Now I avoid not only grizzly bears but also black bears.
sentences.zh: 现在我不仅避开灰熊，也避开黑熊。

sentences.en: Or a wolf attacks me.
sentences.zh: 或者狼攻击了我。

sentences.en: Now I avoid all different kinds of wolves.
sentences.zh: 现在我避开所有不同种类的狼。

sentences.en: And for people who have been in war or near explosions or gun violence or shootings, the loud noise is associated with something horrific and dangerous.
sentences.zh: 对于那些经历过战争、爆炸、枪支暴力或枪击事件的人来说，巨大的噪音与可怕和危险的事物联系在一起。

sentences.en: And now any unpredictable loud noise can create the same response.
sentences.zh: 现在，任何不可预测的巨大噪音都可能产生同样的反应。

sentences.en: And the brain overgeneralizes the fear response to any loud noise, whether it's a slamming door or the fireworks.
sentences.zh: 大脑将恐惧反应过度泛化到任何巨大的噪音上，无论是关门声还是烟花声。

sentences.en: And that's why a lot of veterans and survivors of gun violence, they are terrified of 4th of July, and they try to wear headphones, go to the basement,
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么许多退伍军人和枪支暴力幸存者对7月4日感到恐惧，他们试图戴上耳机，躲进地下室，

sentences.en: because they logically know they are safe.
sentences.zh: 因为他们在逻辑上知道自己是安全的。

sentences.en: This is not the war environment, or this is not the shooting context.
sentences.zh: 这不是战争环境，也不是枪击背景。

sentences.en: The problem is that we are talking about the illogical part of the brain, which basically learns fear through association.
sentences.zh: 问题在于我们谈论的是大脑中不合逻辑的部分，它基本上是通过联想来学习恐惧的。

sentences.en: And I've had even veterans that during the 4th of July, when a firework goes off, they just drop on the floor.
sentences.zh: 我甚至遇到过一些退伍军人，在7月4日烟花燃放时，他们会直接趴在地上。

sentences.en: One of the things that you mentioned about the patient you had who was very successful coming out of college but gradually started to withdraw into himself is that fear tends to cause us to avoid the things that made us fearful.
sentences.zh: 你提到的一位病人，他大学毕业后非常成功，但逐渐开始自我封闭，你提到恐惧往往会导致我们回避那些让我们感到恐惧的事物。

sentences.en: Can you tell me the story of one of your patients who was robbed at a gas station and the effect this later on had on the patient's life?
sentences.zh: 你能讲讲你的一位病人的故事吗？他在加油站被抢劫，这对他的生活产生了什么影响？

sentences.en: Yeah, so when something dangerous happens,
sentences.zh: 是的，当危险的事情发生时，

sentences.en: these highly dangerous, painful situations are very strongly registered.
sentences.zh: 这些高度危险、痛苦的情况会被非常强烈地记录下来。

sentences.en: So for this person, when the robbing happened, they were in the gas station,
sentences.zh: 对于这个人来说，抢劫发生时，他们正在加油站，

sentences.en: they were just about to get in their car,
sentences.zh: 正准备上车，

sentences.en: somebody comes pointing the gun at them and then takes their money.
sentences.zh: 有人用枪指着他们，然后抢走了钱。

sentences.en: This was very terrifying.
sentences.zh: 这非常可怕。

sentences.en: And now this brain wants to prevent this from happening again, right?
sentences.zh: 现在大脑想要防止这种情况再次发生，对吧？

sentences.en: The same story as the grizzly bear.
sentences.zh: 和灰熊的故事一样。

sentences.en: I don't want to be attacked by a grizzly bear again and lose another limb to them.
sentences.zh: 我不想再被灰熊攻击并失去另一条肢体。

sentences.en: So now the brain tries to collect not only data about the bear, but also about the context.
sentences.zh: 所以现在大脑不仅试图收集关于熊的数据，还收集关于背景的数据。

sentences.en: In what context did this happen?
sentences.zh: 这发生在什么背景下？

sentences.en: That corner of the woods, there are bears there.
sentences.zh: 树林的那个角落，那里有熊。

sentences.en: I shouldn't go there anymore.
sentences.zh: 我不应该再去那里了。

sentences.en: Same applies here.
sentences.zh: 这里也一样。

sentences.en: It was a gas station.
sentences.zh: 那是加油站。

sentences.en: It was at this time of the day.
sentences.zh: 那是当天的那个时间。

sentences.en: So the associations becomes the gas stations here for this person.
sentences.zh: 所以对这个人来说，联想就变成了加油站。

sentences.en: Avoiding gas stations, finding it very difficult going there.
sentences.zh: 回避加油站，发现去那里非常困难。

sentences.en: And it's automatic.
sentences.zh: 而且这是自动的。

sentences.en: Logically, they know that the guy with the gun is not at this gas station.
sentences.zh: 逻辑上，他们知道那个拿枪的人不在这个加油站。

sentences.en: Now there may even be cops nearby.
sentences.zh: 现在附近甚至可能有警察。

sentences.en: but they find it difficult.
sentences.zh: 但他们仍然觉得困难。

sentences.en: Gradually, they can expand to convenience stores
sentences.zh: 逐渐地，这种恐惧会扩展到便利店，

sentences.en: or that time of the day.
sentences.zh: 或者那个时间段。

sentences.en: For a lot of people, it's the time of the day
sentences.zh: 对许多人来说，是发生这件事的时间，

sentences.en: or the time of the year that this happened,
sentences.zh: 或者是发生这件事的季节，

sentences.en: that the anxiety increases
sentences.zh: 焦虑感会增加。

sentences.en: because amazingly, the context is not just the physical context,
sentences.zh: 因为令人惊奇的是，语境不仅仅是物理语境，

sentences.en: but also social context, but also temporal context.
sentences.zh: 还包括社会语境，以及时间语境。

sentences.en: From an evolutionary perspective,
sentences.zh: 从进化的角度来看，

sentences.en: let's say you encounter a bear in one neck of the woods.
sentences.zh: 假设你在某片树林里遇到了一只熊。

sentences.en: You now give that area a wide berth.
sentences.zh: 你现在会尽量避开那个区域。

sentences.en: The more often you avoid that area, the better off you're going to be.
sentences.zh: 你避开那个区域的次数越多，你就越安全。

sentences.en: But that same adaptation in the modern context can mean that people quickly cut themselves off
sentences.zh: 但同样的适应机制在现代环境下，可能意味着人们会迅速切断

sentences.en: from everyday sources of meaning and connection.
sentences.zh: 自己与日常意义和联系来源的接触。

sentences.en: So if we avoid a grizzly bear in the woods, every time we avoid it, it's a benefit.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我们避开树林里的灰熊，每次避开都是一种获益。

sentences.en: But the challenge is a lot of these fears that we have learned are context-dependent.
sentences.zh: 但挑战在于，我们学到的许多恐惧都是依赖于语境的。

sentences.en: A loud noise just in the war zone or in a shooting environment is a dangerous thing, right?
sentences.zh: 在战区或枪击环境中，巨大的噪音是危险的，对吧？

sentences.en: On the 4th of July, it's a fun experience.
sentences.zh: 但在7月4日（独立日），那却是一种有趣的体验。

sentences.en: The problem is that sometimes this thing that we're avoiding, for instance, now, in this example, new other gas stations, it's not dangerous.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，有时我们正在避开的这种事物——比如现在这个例子里的加油站——其实并不危险。

sentences.en: But the way it works is that I see it, I freak out because the brain says, this is dangerous, you shouldn't go there.
sentences.zh: 但它的运作方式是：我看到了它，我就惊慌失措，因为大脑说：这很危险，你不应该去那里。

sentences.en: You don't go there, nothing bad happens.
